Senior UN Officials Join IFLA to Strengthen Library Advocacy: From Global Commitments to Local Action by Loida Garcia-Febo Chair, IFLA Management of Library Associations Section (2023–Present) Abstract This article examines one example of how IFLA, its Sections, and its members contribute to strengthening library advocacy by connecting global development commitments with local action. It highlights two online events held by the IFLA Management of Library Associations Section (MLAS) in September and October 2026, featuring senior United Nations officials and library leaders from across regions. The discussions explored how library associations can influence policy, navigate diverse political contexts, build strategic partnerships, and demonstrate libraries’ contributions to sustainable development. Drawing on international experiences, the article identifies key strategies for effective advocacy, including evidence-based engagement, coalition-building, and sustained participation in policymaking. It also underscores the importance of strong library associations in ensuring that libraries’ contributions and community needs are reflected in national, regional, and global development agendas, particularly as the international community looks toward the 2030 Agenda and priorities beyond 2030. title: University Presses Unite as AI and Financial Pressures Threaten Scholarly Publishing (Launch of University Press Charter)
raw_text: From a Joint Statement (Full Text): The University Press Charter unites university presses for the first time behind a commitment to shape a better future for scholarly publishing, at a time when trust, quality and public value-for-money are under threat. Launched during University Press Week (9-13 November) , the Charter has been founded by seven university presses, in a collaboration led by Cambridge University Press and Bristol University Press. It sets out the unique contribution that university presses make to scholarship, higher education, innovation and society. Mandy Hill, Managing Director, Cambridge University Press, said: “Pressures on the academic publishing ecosystem are significant. Real risks are emerging as more papers are created more quickly, with some publishers not prioritising rigorous peer review and as a result content is being trusted less widely. Something has to change. “It’s not too late to reshape the future of academic publishing. Doing what we have always done will not be enough. It is critical that this change is driven by what academics need – and university presses can play a crucial role in this. It’s our responsibility to do so.” Since its circulation, 108 publishers from 26 countries have signed up to the Charter . Translations into French, Portuguese and Welsh are also being prepared by Les Éditions Universitaires de l’Afrique Centrale, Associação Brasileira das Editoras Universitárias and University of Wales Press. title: Gemini Decisions API
raw_text: Gemini Decisions API Google join Jev and OpenAI in the decision model category with "Gemini Decision 1". This new model API is almost identical to Jev: it supports the same three types of questions (yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring) and even reuses Jev's term "Noul" for a yes/no question. It's priced the same as the GPT-6 Luna decision model: 10 cents per million input tokens, and output is free. Jev remains the cheapest of the three, at 4.2 cents per million. Jev is text (and JSON) only. OpenAI can handle text and images. Gemini Decision 1 is fully multi-model: it covers text, images, audio, video, and PDFs. I tested it against video by passing these questions to it along with my Yonkers stomping robot video file: dragon: Does this video have a dragon in it? robot: Does this video have a robot in it? france: Is this video set in France? usa: Is this video set in the USA? Jev and OpenAI both return 1.0 or 0.0 for yes/no questions, but Gemini insists on being a little less confident than that: { "dragon" : { "type" : " yes_no " , "probability" : 0.04976021841520312 }, "robot" : { "type" : " yes_no " , "probability" : 0.9234055387792485 }, "france" : { "type" : " yes_no " , "probability" : 0.08329171353166241 }, "usa" : { "type" : " yes_no " , "probability" : 0.9230459995157706 } } Via Hacker News Tags: ai , generative-ai , gemini , llm-release , jev , decision-models

title: aws-emulator
raw_text: aws-emulator Finally, an official emulator from AWS to run tests against a local clone of their many different services without having to provision a paid API key to do so. It's written in Rust by a huge swarm of agents - 29,684 commits in the first three weeks of the project. Swaminathan (Swami) Sivasubramanian wrote about how it came to be in a guest post on Werner Vogels' blog. It currently requires Docker to run on macOS or Windows. I'm hoping they fix that in the future - it would be great if you could download a single binary and use that as part of a standard test suite in other languages and on other platforms. title: llm 0.37.2
raw_text: Release: llm 0.37.2 Fixes a security issue reported by Daniel de Araujo in GHSA-v9h7-jj4g-f862 and GHSA-r639-rr7r-x72w . LLM has a mechanism called extra-openai-models.yaml - now managed by the new-in-0.37 llm openai endpoint add command - for using LLM with OpenAI-compatible API endpoints from other providers. Daniel reported two ways this could accidentally send your configured OpenAI API key to one of those providers: if the key named by api_key_name had never been stored, or if a responses: true model was run with -o chat_completions 1 . raw_text: It’s that time of year again: Thousands of delegates, lobbyists, and journalists are gathered for the annual UN climate talks, taking place this time in Antalya, Turkey. COP31 officially kicked off on November 8, marking the beginning of negotiations on one of the biggest stages of the climate world. Turkey and Australia are cohosting this year’s talks, which are scheduled to wrap up on November 20. This annual gathering can often serve as an indicator of where the world stands on addressing and adapting to the climate crisis. And this year’s talks are sure to be a doozy—expect a lot of back and forth on fossil fuels and climate finance in particular. Here’s what you should know about COP31. In recent years, the tension always feels high when COP rolls around. (COP stands for “Conference of the Parties.”) But this year feels especially charged: The world is still grappling with the ongoing war in Iran, which has disrupted the Middle East and sent economic shock waves around the world as energy prices have spiked. This year’s COP will be the second without a formal delegation from the US. President Trump formally withdrew the country from the Paris Agreement earlier this year and is in the process of withdrawing from the UN Framework Committee on Climate Change. That’s the treaty that allows formal participation in negotiations. To preserve that elusive continuity of self, some far-thinking technologists are exploring ways to keep the brain going, even beyond death. Their ideas range from freezing brains in liquid nitrogen to augmenting living ones and uploading our memories to the cloud. Ik heb er zin in!” De Raad van Toezicht is verheugd over de benoeming van Ruesen. Hij ontwikkelt een benadering waarin kennisorganisatiesystemen worden beschouwd als veranderlijke modellen die mede richting geven aan ons begrip van de wereld. title: In memoriam Frans van Paassen
raw_text: Op 4 november heeft ons het verdrietige nieuws bereikt dat de heer Frans van Paassen is overleden. Frans van Paassen heeft 16 jaar de functie van secretaris/penningmeester bekleed in het bestuur van ECP. Zijn bijdrage aan ECP is buitengewoon waardevol geweest. Met enorme inzet, betrokkenheid en juist ook de juiste distantie heeft Frans van Paassen de financiële bedrijfsvoering van ECP bewaakt. Hij zorgde met zijn kennis, rust en loyaliteit voor een belangrijke basis van vertrouwen rond het uitdijende werkveld van ECP. De onderwerpen rond digitalisering die ECP organiseert en behandelt kende ook zijn inhoudelijke interesse. Hij woonde bijna alle bijeenkomsten die ECP organiseert bij, waardoor hij niet alleen de financiële processen beoordeelde maar ook inhoudelijk gesprekspartner was voor de medewerkers, het bestuur en het relatienetwerk van ECP. De loyaliteit en inzet voor ECP van Frans van Paassen was een grote steun juist ook in recente tijden waarin ECP zich gaat reorganiseren richting een moderne governance-structuur. Bestuur, directie en medewerkers zijn Frans van Paassen veel dank verschuldigd. Wij zullen Frans met zijn aimabele en betrokken persoonlijkheid zeer gaan missen en wensen zijn dierbaren veel sterkte toe in deze voor hen zo verdrietige periode. raw_text: T-Mobile violated a New York state law by imposing a 50GB-per-month data cap and reducing speeds to less than a megabit per second on home Internet plans it is required to offer people with low incomes, New York government officials alleged. T-Mobile agreed to a settlement requiring it to scrap the data and speed limits, to offer the required low-income plans to more parts of the state, and to make it easier for customers to find information about the plans. The settlement requires T-Mobile to eliminate the speed limits and expand availability of the plans within 120 days. The alleged legal violation and the settlement are related to T-Mobile's wireless home Internet service, not the company's mobile plans. Governor Kathy Hochul and New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the settlement on Monday, saying that a state investigation found T-Mobile violated the New York Affordable Broadband Act (ABA). raw_text: Anduril Industries has announced the successful demonstration of a new satellite-based sensor designed to track other spacecraft that may be hiding their maneuvers in Earth's shadow. Funded with Anduril's internal capital, the company's oven-sized satellite launched on a SpaceX rideshare mission in July with a package of tech demo payloads: an edge-compute processor, a power-management system adaptable to different mission types, and a long-wave infrared space sensor capable of detecting other objects in orbit. Anduril reported on the success of the tech demo mission Tuesday. The company's satellite, named Anduril-216, flies about 590 km (366 mi) above Earth, spending about one-third of each orbit in darkness. Anduril-216's night passes allow its infrared imager to shine. title: Trump admin loses fight to spy on random journalists’ LinkedIn DMs
raw_text: The Trump administration’s fight to stop suspected leaks of top-secret military information on LinkedIn can’t sweep in “a vast number of confidential sources” of random journalists “who have no conceivable relationship” to the Department of Justice’s investigation, an appeals court ruled Tuesday. The order came after the DOJ asked LinkedIn to turn over 18 months of communications from targeted journalists who collectively published more than 1,000 articles on many different topics over that time period. The request was not limited to journalists involved in a controversial report from a news outlet that Trump said exposed confidential military information in a foreign country. (The outlet is not being named to protect national security secrets.) Instead, the DOJ cast a wide net, requesting extensive LinkedIn data on journalists who had any possible link to the journalists around the time the report was drafted. The majority of journalists have LinkedIn accounts and publish their contact information to encourage sources to connect on the platform, LinkedIn argued. So allowing that government overreach went beyond harming targeted journalists and threatened to undermine a critical platform where journalists frequently connect with confidential sources, judges ruled. Even more concerning, the Trump administration secured a secrecy order barring LinkedIn from telling anyone about the sweeping request for a year. title: Big Walk used AI to fix a bug. Now the indie gaming world is having a reckoning.
raw_text: The last few years have seen significant debate over the widespread use of AI-powered tools in game development and the responsible disclosure of that usage to players. That debate has exploded into a full-blown controversy in the indie game development space this week, as Big Walk developer House House has publicly and belatedly disclosed minimal AI use in its popular co-operative puzzle exploration game. This particular controversy has been brewing behind the scenes for months, as judges and jury members for the prestigious Independent Games Festival Awards discussed the issue in private discussion groups. But the debate started to break into public view on Monday when 19 members of the 50-plus-member jury released a signed statement outlining a stance "declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity." Noting "a significant increase in the number of submitted games developer with generative AI tools," the group of jurors called out AI's ecological, economic, psychological, and labor harms in rejecting tools whose use, they said, is still "not a foregone conclusion in our industry." title: Apple is shuttering its 28-year-old online community forum
raw_text: Apple’s online community forum will close on November 20. On Tuesday night, Apple posted a message to the Apple Support Community announcing the forum's closure: The Apple Support Community will permanently close on November 20, 2026. Starting today, the site will no longer accept new posts and is available in a read-only state. You can continue to find trusted guidance and support on the official Apple Support site . We want to thank the community members who have contributed their time and expertise to help others with their Apple products. For 28 years, the forum has provided Apple users with a way to get quick technical advice about their products. title: IBM to offer access to a dual-processor quantum system in 2027
raw_text: IBM's Quantum Developer's Conference is being held this week, and the company is using the gathering to provide an update to its roadmap: It is aiming to make error-corrected quantum computers before the decade is out. The changes greatly expand the scope of its next-generation Nighthawk general-use processors by adding a version with over 500 programmable qubits. At the same time, it's stepping back a bit on its plan to link multiple Nighthawk processors together, dropping the intended number of linked systems from nine to two. title: Show HN: Klad, a paint app your coding agent can drive (source-available)
raw_text: I've been developing applications for a long time and have turned to game development as well lately. One of the things that frustrated me the most was that using AI agents for game development is very annoying in the art department. Your only options right now are to either use an image genAI model and roll the dice every time you want to make an edit, or have your agent draw with something like vectors. I was looking for an application that would allow me to ask an agent to make a first draft of whatever art I needed with actual brushes, and then be able to go in myself and edit every last stroke or layer that it created. Klad is that application. Written in Rust, it can be fully controlled by an agent through the CLI, and every function is available in a nice UI as well: a brush engine, frame-by-frame animation (and bones/IK), vectors, text layers, colours, layer effects, infinite undo (even after re-opening the file!),… Why I think it's useful for a wider audience: Adobe showed agents editing Photoshop files at MAX this week, with a private beta planned for early 2027. title: Show HN: Yogurt – Free, private, open-source alternative to Granola
raw_text: Hey HN, I’m Eric and I want to share an OSS project that I’ve been building in my free time. Yogurt is a free, MIT licensed desktop app that uses on-device AI models to transcribe, summarize, and chat with your meetings. Here's a quick demo video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BFfbXAwRq98 Similar to Granola, Yogurt runs in the background and does not join your calls. But unlike Granola, Yogurt is open-source, free to use, and private. Your meeting transcripts, call recordings, and summaries never leave your computer. As small OSS models have gotten faster and more powerful, Yogurt seemed like a pretty obvious win for privacy and cost conscious folks. You do not need a frontier model to summarize meeting notes or answer questions about them. And if you want to make your notes available to a frontier model, you can just share it with Anthropic, OpenAI, etc. directly via Yogurt’s local MCP server. There’s no need to use a paid cloud service as a middleman. I tried some of the most popular OSS note taking tools, and most were missing features like calendar integration, MCP server, etc. or required you to connect or create an account. title: Trump wanted little Kei trucks for America, Toyota makes it happen
raw_text: The idea that Americans should be offered a greater choice of smaller cars has support from strange bedfellows indeed. After all, who could forget President Trump—usually one to take a maximalist approach to any problem— announcing last year that he wanted the Department of Transportation to make Japan’s diminutive “Kei” cars legal here in the US. Ars’ attempts to get DoT to tell us more about the potential influx of little vehicles have mostly fallen on deaf ears. But this week, there has been movement on the topic, with Toyota announcing that it will bring back the Scion brand with the KEI-01. What’s a Kei car? In the US, the preponderance of humongous SUVs is a consequence largely of government policies, specifically corporate average fuel economy standards that made it less profitable to sell smaller, efficient cars. Japan’s Kei cars are what happens if the government instead restricts the size, engine capacity, and power output. Read full article Comments
